message.content:
{
  "title": "The Kalam Tribunal: Mu'tazili vs Ash'ari",
  "design_thesis": "A high-stakes legal exam where the protagonist must adjudicate live cases by balancing Mu'tazili emphasis on divine justice and human agency against Ash'ari emphasis on divine omnipotence and created causality, forcing the player to choose between moral clarity and theological safety.",
  "core_variables": [
    {
      "id": "doctrinal_alignment",
      "meaning": "Current leaning toward Mu'tazili (Justice/Agency) or Ash'ari (Omnipotence/Causality) affecting available arguments."
    },
    {
      "id": "case_stakes",
      "meaning": "Severity of the legal outcome (e.g., execution, exile, fines) driving the urgency of the ruling."
    },
    {
      "id": "evidence_type",
      "meaning": "Nature of the proof presented (e.g., created ink, physical fire, witnessed oath) determining causal interpretation."
    },
    {
      "id": "theological_risk",
      "meaning": "Potential penalty for violating tawhid or compromising divine attributes during the ruling."
    },
    {
      "id": "human_responsibility",
      "meaning": "Degree of agency attributed to the accused in the current ruling logic."
    }
  ],
  "exam_question_bank": [
    "Is the thief blameworthy if God created the impulse to steal?",
    "Does the eternal nature of the Qur'anic text imply a second eternal entity alongside God?",
    "Can a judge rule against a ruler without compromising divine sovereignty?",
    "Is the fire that burns the scribe a created effect or a direct divine act?",
    "Does affirming God's 'hearing' as a distinct attribute multiply gods or clarify His nature?",
    "Is the widow's loss a result of her own negligence or divine decree?",
    "Can a soldier's oath be binding if all actions are ultimately created by God?",
    "Does interpreting anthropomorphic verses figuratively preserve justice or obscure truth?",
    "Is the physician's cure a natural cause or a pattern of divine will?",
    "Does punishing the heretic uphold justice or threaten divine unity?",
    "Can the written law be created ink while the divine command is eternal?",
    "Is the famine a test of human responsibility or a direct divine punishment?"
  ],
  "scene_ladder": [
    "The Opening Gavel: Establishing the Tribunal's Jurisdiction",
    "The Thief's Confession: Agency vs. Divine Creation",
    "The Ink Dispute: Created Text vs. Eternal Word",
    "The Widow's Appeal: Negligence and Divine Decree",
    "The Soldier's Oath: Causality in the Army",
    "The Ruler's Edict: Sovereignty and Judicial Independence",
    "The Physician's Cure: Natural Causes and Divine Patterns",
    "The Fire Trial: Direct Action vs. Secondary Effects",
    "The Heretic's Defense: Figurative Language and Literal Truth",
    "The Judge's Dilemma: Justice vs. Theological Safety",
    "The Scribe's Accusation: Written Law and Divine Command",
    "The Famine Debate: Testing or Punishment?",
    "The Widow's Return: Final Ruling on Responsibility",
    "The Scholar's Challenge: Attributes and Essence",
    "The Prisoner's Plea: Voluntary Acts and Moral Clarity",
    "The Oath Breaker: Binding Words and Divine Will",
    "The Final Appeal: Balancing the Two Schools",
    "The Verdict: Synthesis of Justice and Omnipotence"
  ],
  "secret_route": "The player discovers that both schools serve a protective function: Mu'tazili doctrine guards against arbitrary tyranny by insisting on human accountability, while Ash'ari doctrine guards against reducing God to a mere mechanism by insisting on His ultimate creative power. By ruling not on which side is 'right' but on which school's logic best protects the specific human life before them, the player achieves a
